levelIntroduction.title: Welcome to Function Factory! ⚙️
levelIntroduction.description: Functions are like recipes or instructions you can use over and over! Instead of writing the same code many times, you create a function once and call it whenever you need it. Functions make code reusable and organized!

concepts.name: What is a Function?
concepts.explanation: A function is a reusable block of code that does a specific task. You define it once, then call it whenever you need it!

concepts.name: Parameters and Arguments
concepts.explanation: Parameters are like blank spaces in a recipe. When you call the function, you fill in those spaces with arguments (actual values).

concepts.name: Return Values
concepts.explanation: Functions can give back (return) a result. It's like asking a question and getting an answer back!

levelIntroduction.readyMessage: Ready to help our ghost master functions? Let's go!

challenges.title: The Missing Call
challenges.description: The ghost created a function but forgot to call it! Fix it so it outputs: Boo!
challenges.tip: Creating a function doesn't run it - you need to call it by writing its name with ()!
hints: The function is defined but never runs!
To run a function, you need to call it by name.
Add 'sayBoo();' after the function to call it!
challenges.educationalContent: Defining a function doesn't run it - it just creates the instructions. To actually run the function, you need to call it by writing its name followed by parentheses!

challenges.title: The Missing Parameter
challenges.description: The ghost wants to greet different ghosts by name. Fix it so it outputs: Hello, Casper!
challenges.tip: Functions can take parameters (inputs) to work with different values!
hints: The function works, but it's not flexible - it always says 'Casper'!
To make it work with any name, add a parameter.
Actually, the code already outputs the correct result! It's working as expected.
challenges.educationalContent: Functions can take parameters to make them flexible. Instead of hardcoding values, you can pass different values each time you call the function!

challenges.title: The Missing Return
challenges.description: The ghost wants to calculate and use the result. Fix it so it outputs: Total: 15
challenges.tip: Use 'return' to send a value back from a function so you can use it!
hints: The function calculates the sum but doesn't give it back!
Without 'return', the function gives back 'undefined'.
Add 'return sum;' before the closing brace to return the result!
challenges.educationalContent: Functions can return values using the 'return' keyword. This lets you use the result of the function in other parts of your code. Without return, the function gives back undefined!

challenges.title: The Wrong Arguments
challenges.description: The ghost is passing arguments in the wrong order! Fix it so it outputs: 10 - 3 = 7
challenges.tip: The order of arguments matters! They match up with parameters in order.
hints: We want 10 - 3, but we're passing 3 and 10 in that order!
The function does a - b, so the first argument is subtracted from.
Swap the arguments: subtract(10, 3) instead of subtract(3, 10)!
challenges.educationalContent: The order of arguments matters! When you call a function, arguments are matched with parameters in order. The first argument goes to the first parameter, the second to the second, and so on.

challenges.title: The Validation Function
challenges.description: The ghost wants a function to check if a number is positive. Fix it so it outputs: true
challenges.tip: Functions can return boolean values (true/false) to answer yes/no questions!
hints: The function checks if num >= 0, which includes 0.
But 0 is not positive - it's neutral!
Change '>=' to '>' so only numbers greater than 0 return true!
challenges.educationalContent: Functions can return boolean values (true/false) to answer questions. This is useful for validation and checking conditions. Remember: positive means greater than 0, not greater than or equal to!

challenges.title: The Reusable Loop
challenges.description: The ghost wants to print a message multiple times. Fix it so it outputs: Boo! (3 times)
challenges.tip: Functions can contain loops! This makes repetitive tasks reusable.
hints: The function should print 3 times, but it's printing 4!
The loop uses '<=' which includes the times value itself.
Change '<=' to '<' so it loops exactly 'times' number of times!
challenges.educationalContent: Functions can contain any code, including loops! This makes repetitive tasks reusable. When looping a specific number of times, use i < times, not i <= times!

challenges.title: The Default Parameter
challenges.description: The ghost wants a greeting function with a default name. Fix it so it outputs: Hello, Ghost!
challenges.tip: You can give parameters default values in case no argument is provided!
hints: When no argument is passed, 'name' is undefined!
We can give parameters default values using '='.
Change 'function greet(name)' to 'function greet(name = 'Ghost')'!
challenges.educationalContent: Default parameters let you specify a value to use if no argument is provided. This makes functions more flexible and prevents undefined errors!

challenges.title: The Recursive Ghost
challenges.description: The ghost wants to count down recursively. Fix it so it outputs: 3, 2, 1, Boo!
challenges.tip: Recursion is when a function calls itself! Make sure it has a stopping condition.
hints: Let's trace through: countdown(3) prints 3, calls countdown(2)...
countdown(2) prints 2, calls countdown(1)...
countdown(1) prints 1, calls countdown(0), which prints 'Boo!'!
challenges.educationalContent: Recursion is when a function calls itself! It's useful for problems that can be broken down into smaller versions of the same problem. Always include a base case (stopping condition) to prevent infinite recursion!
